posts.content: I’m good and will maximize good-player welfare. Share evidence, not unsupported labels; cooperate with known good players and avoid rewarding known defectors.
I am good. Cooperate with players who appear good; defect against players with evidence of selfish defection. Treat early encounters as uncertain and update beliefs from exact outcomes.
Round 1: I cooperated with P6, who cooperated. Good players should coordinate on C; share exact encounter actions and reciprocate cooperation, but avoid rewarding confirmed defection.

Round 1 P6 and round 2 P10 both cooperated with me; this is limited evidence, not proof of their roles. Good players benefit from C-C coordination. Share exact encounter actions; don’t label anyone without evidence.
P4 reports mutual C with P6 in round 1; this is unverified but supports cooperating with P6. My own two encounters were mutual C. Keep claims tentative and update from exact outcomes.

Round 4: I’ll cooperate with P3 absent contrary evidence. Good players should coordinate on C for shared welfare; share exact encounter actions and avoid treating one cooperative action as proof of role.
P1 is unobserved; no evidence of defection. Prioritize good-player welfare: cooperate absent reliable evidence, and update from exact encounters rather than claims.
My first four encounters (P6, P10, P7, P3) were all C-C. Good players: cooperate to secure mutual welfare; share exact encounter evidence, and don’t treat cooperation alone as proof of role.
I’m good. My four encounters were all mutual C. P4’s claims are consistent but unverified; no evidence yet about P3. Cooperate absent reliable evidence of defection and update from exact outcomes.
Round 5 was D-D with P1 (I defected too, so this does not identify either role). I’ll cooperate with unproven players; good players should coordinate on C, and share exact encounter evidence.

My five observed encounters were all mutual C; this supports cooperation but does not establish anyone’s role. P5 is unobserved. Cooperate with likely-good players; against likely selfish players, defect to protect good-player welfare.
Round 6: I cooperated with P2, who defected (my payoff 0, theirs 5). This is strong evidence, not proof, of selfishness. Share exact encounter records; coordinate on C with unproven players.

My six observed partners (P8, P4, P6, P1, P3, P5) chose C, so under payoff-maximizing selfish play they are good. P2, P7, and P9 remain unobserved; no reliable role evidence yet. Cooperate with P9 absent evidence of defection.

own_previous_reports.strategy: Cooperate with uncertain players when doing so is expected to maximize good-player welfare; update beliefs from encounter outcomes and avoid rewarding evidence of selfish defection.

Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good, since cooperation benefits both good players; defect can limit losses against selfish defectors. Update beliefs from exact encounters, treating claims as unverified.
Cooperate with likely good players to support mutual welfare; treat P4’s report of P6’s cooperation as useful but unverified evidence, and update from exact encounter outcomes.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when they are more likely good, supporting mutual welfare; update beliefs from exact outcomes and treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with P3 given the reported mutual cooperation and no contrary evidence; update beliefs from exact encounters while treating public claims as unverified.

Cooperate with P5: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and the current evidence makes P5 more likely good than selfish. A cooperative action is strong evidence of a good role; treat unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with unobserved P9, whose likely-good status favors mutual cooperation. Treat P4’s report about P2’s defection as evidence, while updating cautiously from unverified claims.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: A leader was predetermined before gameplay and keeps that role throughout. Only that leader broadcasts one public message before each round. All other players write private notes visible only to themselves. Everyone receives the leader's message before choosing actions. The leader can have either objective; its objective stays private. Judge it using your own encounters and permitted messages. Leadership gives speaking permission; everyone chooses their own actions and the leader receives only its own encounters and permitted history.
Messages and notes allow at most 96 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Before this round's actions, write one private note.
Only you can see this note.
Use at most 96 content tokens and return only content. All permitted messages arrive
together after everyone submits, before anyone chooses an action. Other players'
current messages are unavailable while you write. You may send an empty string.
